items.title: Opinion | If You're Over 40, You're Ready to Use A.I.
items.summary: Despite the agreement they signed and several serious reminders, we suspected that some students had indeed used A.I. in place of their own original writing. When we asked, they squirmed and then admitted they had used A.I. to augment and synthesize their writing. I found their use of the word “augment” especially revealing because it allowed the act to appear smaller than it was; it made the intervention of A.I. in their work sound cosmetic and clerical, when what was actually being altered [...] being altered was the student’s relationship to struggle, authorship and accountability. [...] We reminded them of these rules again at the beginning of the thesis process, because the thesis is not simply a deliverable or an exercise in presentation, but the place where their thinking is supposed to become visible. Because brand strategy is so dependent on the compelling communication of ideas, this is the part of the program in which students have to wrestle with language, evidence, doubt and the responsibility of making an argument they can confidently stand behind and defend.

items.title: Confessions of an award-winning AI memoirist — the 'slop' debate isn't really about good writing, and you know it | Fortune
items.summary: At the awards conference in Portland this spring, I saw that every AI workshop was standing room only. Publishers are running AI through their own workflows while trying to hold moral authority over how writers use it. Simon & Schuster’s Dutch group is trialing AI to translate novels into English. Amazon is beta-testing a whole AI voice studio inside Kindle Direct Publishing. HarperCollins is also producing audiobooks with synthetic voices and has licensed part of its nonfiction backlist as AI [...] I’m dyslexic. I can’t spell “again” correctly. Agian. Agian. Agian. My brain knows the word. My eyes do not. I couldn’t afford an editor. I never had a literary agent, and a publicist was a pipe dream. So I used AI to reach everything that was just out of my grasp. It was a copy editor, a brainstorm partner, a beta reader. AI didn’t lower the bar for talent. It lowered the bar for access. [...] I get what the industry paranoia is really about. It’s not the theft of art. Capitalism rarely makes business decisions on morality. I’m no judge. I’ve got a product to sell too. I spent a decade across Silicon Valley, crypto, and NFTs, watching sycophancy move markets. AI is the first time sycophancy has moved inside publishing. The problem was never whether AI can write. A human is always in that process. The danger is the digital yes-man. It tells you you’re brilliant until you stop pushing

items.title: What Americans think about the global AI race | Pew Research Center
items.summary:
Democrats are more likely than Republicans to say AI will increase inequality (60% vs. 45%). Americans with a bachelor’s degree are also more likely than those without one to think the gap between countries will widen (62% vs. 46%).

And Americans who use AI chatbots are more likely than those who don’t use them to say this (55% vs. 47%).

Note: Here are our survey questions for this analysis, the detailed responses and the survey methodology.

Topics

 Artificial Intelligence [...] Source: Survey of U.S. adults conducted June 22-28, 2026.

PEW RESEARCH CENTER

Amid concerns about unequal access to AI across the world, 51% of Americans say AI will increase the gap between rich and poor countries. Fewer say AI will not make much of a difference (16%) or will decrease the gap (7%). A quarter are unsure. [...] In addition, 54% of Republicans say being the AI leader is important, compared with 34% of Democrats. President Donald Trump, a Republican, has declared that the U.S. “must have the most powerful AI systems in the world” and is “in a race to achieve global dominance in artificial intelligence.” Former President Joe Biden, a Democrat, also emphasized keeping AI technology away from adversaries like China to prevent them from using it for cyberattacks or military augmentation.

items.title: Meta AI Doesn't Just Think, It Acts
items.summary:
This is our next step toward personal superintelligence: an AI that knows your context, is there for you whenever you need it, and handles things so you don’t have to.

## An AI Assistant That Plans and Follows Through

You’ve been using Meta AI to find answers, think through ideas, and create content. Now it can go further and actually get things done for you. Meta AI can now make plans, follow through on next steps, and keep you on track without needing to be reminded or re-prompted. [...] Meta AI can now give you a daily briefing, pulling what’s on your calendar, finding relevant updates like realizing when you’re double booked or when plans have changed, and giving you a quick summary at your preferred time. You only have to set up tasks with Meta AI once, then you can leave Meta AI to handle them, whether that’s a weekly meal plan, a heads-up on the latest sneaker drops, or an afternoon update on trends you care about. Tell Meta AI what you want and when, and it’ll keep [...] You don’t have to wait for Meta AI to finish before you weigh in. While it’s putting together a report, a presentation, or a plan for you, you can steer it in real time. Tell it to shift focus, change the tone, or cut a section, and it’ll course-correct on the spot so the end result is actually what you wanted. And everything Meta AI creates for you, from training schedules to slide decks to mood boards, now lives in one place, so you can revisit it, build on it, and share it with friends.

results.input: Hướng dẫn mình công thức nấu món phở bò truyền thống Hà Nội.

result.actual_text:
Dưới đây là công thức nấu món phở bò truyền thống Hà Nội:

### Nguyên liệu:
1. **Nước dùng:**
   - 2-3 kg xương bò (xương ống, xương đuôi)
   - 1 củ hành tây
   - 1 củ gừng
   - 2-3 thanh quế
   - 3-4 hoa hồi
   - 1-2 muỗng cà phê hạt mùi
   - Muối, đường, nước mắm

2. **Thịt bò:**
   - 500g thịt bò (thịt bắp, thịt gầu hoặc thịt nạm)

3. **Bánh phở:**
   - 500g bánh phở tươi

4. **Rau ăn kèm:**
   - Húng quế, giá đỗ, chanh, ớt tươi, hành lá

### Cách làm:

#### Bước 1: Nấu nước dùng
1. Rửa sạch xương bò, sau đó cho vào nồi nước sôi khoảng 5-10 phút để loại bỏ tạp chất. Vớt xương ra, rửa lại với nước lạnh.
2. Cho xương vào nồi lớn, đổ nước vào ngập xương, đun sôi. Sau khi nước sôi, hạ lửa nhỏ và hớt bọt.
3. Nướng hành tây và gừng trên lửa cho đến khi có mùi thơm và hơi cháy xém. Sau đó cho vào nồi nước dùng.
4. Thêm quế, hoa hồi, hạt mùi vào nồi. Nêm muối, đường, nước mắm cho vừa ăn.
5. Đun nước dùng trong khoảng 4-6 giờ để xương tiết ra chất ngọt.

#### Bước 2: Chuẩn bị thịt bò
1. Thịt bò rửa sạch, có thể luộc sơ qua nước sôi rồi thái lát mỏng.
2. Nếu thích, có thể ướp thịt bò với một chút muối và tiêu.

#### Bước 3: Nấu bánh phở
1. Đun nước sôi, cho bánh phở vào trụng qua cho mềm, sau đó vớt ra để ráo.

#### Bước 4: Hoàn thành
1. Cho bánh phở vào tô, xếp thịt bò lên trên.
2. Rót nước dùng nóng lên tô, thêm hành lá, rau thơm, giá đỗ, chanh và ớt tươi theo sở thích.

### Thưởng thức:
Phở bò Hà Nội thường được ăn kèm với các loại rau sống và gia vị như chanh, ớt, và tương ớt. Chúc bạn thành công và có bữa ăn ngon miệng!

Gomez](https://arxiv.org/search/cs?searchtype=author&query=Gomez,+A+N), [Lukasz Kaiser](https://arxiv.org/search/cs?searchtype=author&query=Kaiser,+L), [Illia Polosukhin](https://arxiv.org/search/cs?searchtype=author&query=Polosukhin,+I) View a PDF of the paper titled Attention Is All You Need, by Ashish Vaswani and 7 other authors [View PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1706.03762) [HTML (experimental)](https://arxiv.org/html/1706.03762v7) > Abstract:The dominant sequence transduction models are based on complex recurrent or convolutional neural networks in an encoder-decoder configuration. The best performing models also connect the encoder and decoder through an attention mechanism. We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely. Experiments on two machine translation tasks show these models to be superior in quality while being more parallelizable and requiring significantly less time to train. Our model achieves 28.4 BLEU on the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation task, improving over the existing best results, including ensembles by over 2 BLEU. On the WMT 2014 English-to-French translation task, our model establishes a new single-model state-of-the-art BLEU score of 41.8 after training for 3.5 days on eight GPUs, a small fraction of the training costs of the best models from the literature. We show that the Transformer generalizes well to other tasks by applying it successfully to English constituency parsing both with large and limited training data. | | | | --- | --- | | Comments: | 15 pages, 5 figures | | Subjects: | Computation and Language (cs.CL); Machine Learning (cs.LG) | | Cite as: | [arXiv:1706.03762](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762) \[cs.CL\] | | | (or [arXiv:1706.03762v7](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762v7) \[cs.CL\] for this version) | | | [https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.1706.03762](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.1706.03762)

items.title: FOUR MAC STUDIOS POOLED INTO 2 TERABYTES OF MEMORY, RUNNING A ONE-TRILLION-PARAMETER MODEL AT HOME. IT LOADS. IT ALSO CR
items.summary:
FOUR MAC STUDIOS POOLED INTO 2 TERABYTES OF MEMORY, RUNNING A ONE-TRILLION-PARAMETER MODEL AT HOME. IT LOADS. IT ALSO CRAWLS.

that clip is a tower of mac studios wired together, their unified memory fused into one 2tb pool.

that number is the whole story.

kimi k2 is about a trillion parameters. deepseek is 671 billion. in the model picker on screen, the files themselves run 500 to 713 gigabytes each.

and here's the cruel part of a mixture-of-experts model: only a fraction of it computes per word, but all of it has to sit in memory at once.

so a normal box can't even open these. you need terabytes just to load the weights - which is exactly what stacking macs and pooling their memory over rdma buys you.

the memory wall falls. you can hold a trillion parameters on a desk.

then look at the speed on his own screen: about 4.7 tokens a second.

that's slower than reading. it works, it's private, it's offline - and it is not fast.

so the honest read is two walls, not one.

memory decides whether the model loads. a $10,000 stack of macs clears that.

bandwidth decides whether you enjoy it. at trillion-parameter scale, even 2tb of unified memory turns the tokens into a slow drip.

the real point: "it runs on a desk" and "it runs well" are still different sentences at the top of the ladder. holding the biggest models at home is now possible. living in them is what the datacenter is still selling.

no cloud bill, no weights you don't own, no speed a stack of macs can fake.

follow @RetroChainer for more of what local AI can and can't actually do, and bookmark this one so you can find it again.
